gloss: castle tower; main keep of a Japanese castle

definitions.explanation: The tall, central tower of a Japanese castle, serving as the final defensive stronghold and the symbolic centerpiece of the fortification. Typically a multi-storied structure with distinctive curved rooflines, it was the most visually striking element of castle architecture during the Sengoku and Edo periods.

notes:
Also written as ⟦{天守閣|てんしゅかく}→天守閣：17449_tenshukaku⟧, which adds the suffix {閣|かく} ('tower; pavilion'). Both forms refer to the same structure, though ⟦{天守閣|てんしゅかく}→天守閣：17449_tenshukaku⟧ is the more common form in everyday conversation and tourist contexts.

ETYMOLOGY:
- Castle keeps emerged during the late Muromachi and Sengoku periods (16th century) as military architecture evolved
- {織田|おだ}{信長|のぶなが}'s {安土城|あづちじょう} (1579) is considered the first grand-scale {天守|てんしゅ}
- Only twelve original {天守|てんしゅ} survive today; many others are reconstructions

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- ⟦{天守閣|てんしゅかく}→天守閣：17449_tenshukaku⟧: castle keep (with pavilion suffix; more common form)
- {天守|てんしゅ}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{登|のぼ}る→登る：00660_noboru⟧: to climb the castle keep
- ⟦{現存|げんそん}→現存：13544_genson⟧{天守|てんしゅ}: surviving original keep
- ⟦{復元|ふくげん}→復元：09249_fukugen⟧{天守|てんしゅ}: reconstructed keep
- {天守台|てんしゅだい}: keep foundation/platform

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{城|しろ}→城：03255_shiro⟧: castle — the general word for a castle as a whole, including walls, moats, and grounds
- ⟦{櫓|やぐら}→櫓：10646_yagura⟧: turret; watchtower — smaller defensive towers positioned at corners or along castle walls
- ⟦{本丸|ほんまる}→本丸：24197_honmaru⟧: main bailey — the innermost fortified area of a castle where the keep stands
